claim: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have identified thousands of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with a wide range of complex traits.
source: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have identified thousands of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with a wide range of complex traits (MacArthur et al., 2017; Visscher et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to MacArthur et al., 2017 and Visscher et al., 2017

claim: Most SNPs implicated by GWASs reside in non-coding regions of the genome.
source: However, the path from GWAS to biology is not straightforward as most SNPs implicated by GWASs reside in non-coding regions of the genome (MacArthur et al., 2017) and do not directly inform on the functional mechanism through which variants exert their effect on phenotypes.
evidence: Supported by citation to MacArthur et al., 2017

claim: SNPs in non-coding regions do not directly inform on the functional mechanism through which variants exert their effect on phenotypes.
source: However, the path from GWAS to biology is not straightforward as most SNPs implicated by GWASs reside in non-coding regions of the genome (MacArthur et al., 2017) and do not directly inform on the functional mechanism through which variants exert their effect on phenotypes.
evidence: Draws from established understanding of non-coding variant interpretation

claim: GWASs have been performed on gene expression identifying genetic variants influencing molecular traits, commonly referred to as molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs).
source: GWASs have been performed on gene expression (Võsa et al., 2021), DNA methylation (Min et al., 2021), protein (Sun et al., 2018), and metabolite (Shin et al., 2014; Lotta et al., 2021) levels, identifying genetic variants influencing molecular traits, commonly referred to as molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Võsa et al., 2021; Min et al., 2021; Sun et al., 2018; Shin et al., 2014; Lotta et al., 2021)

claim: The large overlap between complex and molecular trait-associated variants suggests that integrating these data can help interpreting GWAS loci.
source: The large overlap between complex and molecular trait-associated variants suggests that integrating these data can help interpreting GWAS loci (Vandiedonck, 2018; Taylor et al., 2019; Ongen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vandiedonck, 2018; Taylor et al., 2019; Ongen et al., 2017

claim: Gene expression is the best studied molecular phenotype due to large expression QTL (eQTL) studies.
source: Advances in the field of transcriptomics make gene expression the best studied molecular phenotype, thanks to the presence of large expression QTL (eQTL) studies (e.g., eQTLGen Consortium [Võsa et al., 2021] N>30,000).
evidence: Supported by citation to eQTLGen Consortium (Võsa et al., 2021) with sample size N>30,000

claim: The eQTLGen Consortium has N>30,000 samples.
source: Advances in the field of transcriptomics make gene expression the best studied molecular phenotype, thanks to the presence of large expression QTL (eQTL) studies (e.g., eQTLGen Consortium [Võsa et al., 2021] N>30,000).
evidence: Directly stated sample size for eQTLGen Consortium

claim: Availability of large eQTL datasets fostered the development of summary statistic-based statistical approaches aiming at identifying associations between transcripts and complex traits.
source: Availability of these datasets fostered the development of summary statistic-based statistical approaches aiming at identifying associations between transcripts and complex traits (Zhu et al., 2016; Porcu et al., 2019; Hormozdiari et al., 2014; Gusev et al., 2016), prioritizing genes from known GWAS loci for functional follow-up, and inferring the directionality of these relations (Porcu et al., 2019; Porcu et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple methodological papers (Zhu et al., 2016; Porcu et al., 2019; Hormozdiari et al., 2014; Gusev et al., 2016)

claim: The cascade of events that mediates the effect of genetic variants on complex traits involves more than one molecular trait.
source: However, the cascade of events that mediates the effect of genetic variants on complex traits involves more than one molecular trait.
evidence: Based on understanding of biological pathways and multi-omics relationships

claim: Investigating whether molecular traits reside along the same causal pathway remains under-explored.
source: Although approaches used for gene expression can be extended to other molecular data, investigating whether these molecular traits reside along the same causal pathway remains under-explored and only recently have studies applied colocalization and Mendelian randomization (MR) to methylation, gene expression, and protein levels data (Giambartolomei et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2018; Gleason et al., 2020; Sadler et al., 2022) and to a lesser extent to metabolic QTLs (mQTL) (Yin et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to recent studies (Giambartolomei et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2018; Gleason et al., 2020; Sadler et al., 2022; Yin et al., 2022)

claim: Metabolites are often the final products of cellular regulatory processes.
source: Metabolites are often the final products of cellular regulatory processes and the most proximal omic layer to complex phenotypes.
evidence: Based on established understanding of cellular metabolism and molecular hierarchies

claim: Metabolites are the most proximal omic layer to complex phenotypes.
source: Metabolites are often the final products of cellular regulatory processes and the most proximal omic layer to complex phenotypes.
evidence: Based on understanding of biological information flow from genotype to phenotype

claim: Metabolite levels represent the ultimate response of biological systems to genetic and environmental changes.
source: Their levels could thus represent the ultimate response of biological systems to genetic and environmental changes.
evidence: Logical inference from metabolites being final products of cellular processes

claim: The metabolic status of organisms reflects disease progression.
source: For instance, the metabolic status of organisms reflects disease progression, as metabolic disturbances can often be observed several years prior to the symptomatic phase (Shah et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2011; Sabatine et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Shah et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2011; Sabatine et al., 2005

claim: Metabolic disturbances can often be observed several years prior to the symptomatic phase of disease.
source: For instance, the metabolic status of organisms reflects disease progression, as metabolic disturbances can often be observed several years prior to the symptomatic phase (Shah et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2011; Sabatine et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Shah et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2011; Sabatine et al., 2005

claim: Using metabolomics to identify early-stage biomarkers of complex phenotypes has gained increased interest.
source: Therefore, using metabolomics to identify early-stage biomarkers of complex phenotypes, such as prediabetes and COVID-19 susceptibility, has gained increased interest (Wang-Sattler et al., 2012; Julkunen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wang-Sattler et al., 2012; Julkunen et al., 2021

claim: Two-sample MR approaches using metabolites as single exposure have revealed biomarkers for several diseases.
source: While two-sample MR approaches using metabolites as single exposure have revealed biomarkers for several diseases (Qian et al., 2021; Lord et al., 2021; Porcu et al., 2021a), these analyses focused on the prediction of disease risk rather than on deciphering the mechanisms of discovered associations.
evidence: Supported by citations to Qian et al., 2021; Lord et al., 2021; Porcu et al., 2021a

claim: Previous metabolite MR analyses focused on the prediction of disease risk rather than on deciphering the mechanisms of discovered associations.
source: While two-sample MR approaches using metabolites as single exposure have revealed biomarkers for several diseases (Qian et al., 2021; Lord et al., 2021; Porcu et al., 2021a), these analyses focused on the prediction of disease risk rather than on deciphering the mechanisms of discovered associations.
evidence: Based on characterization of previous studies cited (Qian et al., 2021; Lord et al., 2021; Porcu et al., 2021a)

claim: Integrating transcriptomics with metabolomics data can provide insights into how metabolites are regulated.
source: Integrating transcriptomics with metabolomics data can provide insights into how metabolites are regulated, elucidating targetable functional mechanisms.
evidence: Based on logical inference about multi-omics integration

claim: The study developed a framework based on established MR methodology that hypothesizes a mediating role of the metabolome in the transcript-to-phenotype axis.
source: Here, we develop a framework based on established MR methodology that hypothesizes a mediating role of the metabolome in the transcript-to-phenotype axis, with the primary exposure being defined as an upstream omic layer, namely gene expression.
evidence: Description of the study's methodological approach

claim: The integrative MR analysis combines summary-level multi-omics (GWAS, eQTL, and mQTL) data to compute the indirect effect of gene expression on complex traits mediated by metabolites in three steps.
source: Specifically, our integrative MR analysis combines summary-level multi-omics (i.e., GWAS, eQTL, and mQTL) data to compute the indirect effect of gene expression on complex traits mediated by metabolites in three steps (Figure 1).
evidence: Description of the study's analytical approach with reference to Figure 1

claim: The study identified 216 transcript-metabolite-trait causal triplets involving 26 medically relevant phenotypes.
source: We identified 216 transcript-metabolite-trait causal triplets involving 26 medically relevant phenotypes.
evidence: Primary finding from the study's analysis

claim: 58% of the identified associations were missed by classical transcriptome-wide MR.
source: Among these associations, 58% were missed by classical transcriptome-wide MR, which only uses gene expression and GWAS data.
evidence: Quantitative comparison of methods from the study's results

claim: Classical transcriptome-wide MR only uses gene expression and GWAS data.
source: Among these associations, 58% were missed by classical transcriptome-wide MR, which only uses gene expression and GWAS data.
evidence: Description of the classical TWMR method

claim: The study identified a causal relationship between ANKH and calcium levels mediated by citrate levels.
source: This allowed the identification of biologically relevant pathways, such as between ANKH and calcium levels mediated by citrate levels and SLC6A12 and serum creatinine through modulation of the levels of the renal osmolyte betaine.
evidence: Specific finding from the study's analysis

claim: The study identified a causal relationship between SLC6A12 and serum creatinine through modulation of the levels of the renal osmolyte betaine.
source: This allowed the identification of biologically relevant pathways, such as between ANKH and calcium levels mediated by citrate levels and SLC6A12 and serum creatinine through modulation of the levels of the renal osmolyte betaine.
evidence: Specific finding from the study's analysis

claim: The signals missed by transcriptome-wide MR are found thanks to the increase in power conferred by integrating multiple omics layers.
source: We show that the signals missed by transcriptome-wide MR are found, thanks to the increase in power conferred by integrating multiple omics layer.
evidence: Explanation of methodological advantage from the study

claim: With larger molecular QTL studies and in case of mediated effects, the multi-omics MR framework outperforms classical MR approaches.
source: Simulation analyses show that with larger molecular QTL studies and in case of mediated effects, our multi-omics MR framework outperforms classical MR approaches designed to detect causal relationships between single molecular traits and complex phenotypes.
evidence: Finding from simulation analyses conducted in the study

claim: The study applied univariable MR to identify metabolites whose levels are causally influenced by transcript levels in whole blood.
source: We applied univariable MR to identify metabolites whose levels are causally influenced by transcript levels in whole blood (Figure 1A).
evidence: Description of the study's analytical approach

claim: Summary statistics for cis-eQTLs stem from the eQTLGen Consortium meta-analysis of 19,942 transcripts in 31,684 individuals.
source: Summary statistics for cis-eQTLs stem from the eQTLGen Consortium meta-analysis of 19,942 transcripts in 31,684 individuals (Võsa et al., 2021), while summary statistics for mQTLs originate from a meta-analysis of 453 metabolites in 7824 individuals from two independent European cohorts: TwinsUK (N = 6056) and KORA (N = 1768) (Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: Description of data sources used in the study with citation to Võsa et al., 2021

claim: Summary statistics for mQTLs originate from a meta-analysis of 453 metabolites in 7824 individuals from two independent European cohorts: TwinsUK (N = 6056) and KORA (N = 1768).
source: Summary statistics for cis-eQTLs stem from the eQTLGen Consortium meta-analysis of 19,942 transcripts in 31,684 individuals (Võsa et al., 2021), while summary statistics for mQTLs originate from a meta-analysis of 453 metabolites in 7824 individuals from two independent European cohorts: TwinsUK (N = 6056) and KORA (N = 1768) (Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: Description of data sources used in the study with citation to Shin et al., 2014

claim: The analysis was restricted to 7884 transcripts with ≥3 instrumental variables.
source: After selecting SNPs included in both the eQTL and mQTL studies, our analysis was restricted to 7884 transcripts with ≥3 instrumental variables (IVs) (see Methods, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and 242 metabolites with an identifier in the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) (Wishart et al., 2022) (see Methods, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: Description of filtering criteria applied in the study

claim: The analysis was restricted to 242 metabolites with an identifier in the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB).
source: After selecting SNPs included in both the eQTL and mQTL studies, our analysis was restricted to 7884 transcripts with ≥3 instrumental variables (IVs) (see Methods, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and 242 metabolites with an identifier in the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) (Wishart et al., 2022) (see Methods, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: Description of filtering criteria applied in the study with citation to Wishart et al., 2022

claim: The study detected 96 genes whose transcript levels causally impacted 75 metabolites, resulting in 133 unique transcript-metabolite associations.
source: By testing each gene for association with the 242 metabolites, we detected 96 genes whose transcript levels causally impacted 75 metabolites, resulting in 133 unique transcript-metabolite associations (FDR 5% considering all 1,907,690 instrumentable gene-metabolite pairs; Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: Primary finding from the transcript-to-metabolite analysis

claim: 86% of involved genes were causally influencing the level of a single metabolite.
source: Most involved genes (86%; 83/96) were causally influencing the level of a single metabolite, with some notable exceptions acting as mQTL hubs, such as TMEM258 and FADS2 both affecting the same 11 metabolites, followed by FADS1 affecting a subset of six metabolites.
evidence: Quantitative characterization of transcript-metabolite relationships from the study

claim: TMEM258 and FADS2 both affect the same 11 metabolites.
source: Most involved genes (86%; 83/96) were causally influencing the level of a single metabolite, with some notable exceptions acting as mQTL hubs, such as TMEM258 and FADS2 both affecting the same 11 metabolites, followed by FADS1 affecting a subset of six metabolites.
evidence: Specific finding from the study's analysis

claim: FADS1 affects a subset of six metabolites.
source: Most involved genes (86%; 83/96) were causally influencing the level of a single metabolite, with some notable exceptions acting as mQTL hubs, such as TMEM258 and FADS2 both affecting the same 11 metabolites, followed by FADS1 affecting a subset of six metabolites.
evidence: Specific finding from the study's analysis

claim: Only 5 (3.8%) of the 133 transcript-metabolite associations were reported in HMDB.
source: While only 5 (3.8%) of the 133 associations were reported in HMDB, an automated literature review (see Methods) identified a match for 22 (16.5%) of the identified transcript-metabolite pairs (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: Result from literature validation analysis

claim: An automated literature review identified a match for 22 (16.5%) of the identified transcript-metabolite pairs.
source: While only 5 (3.8%) of the 133 associations were reported in HMDB, an automated literature review (see Methods) identified a match for 22 (16.5%) of the identified transcript-metabolite pairs (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: Result from literature validation analysis

claim: Univariable metabolome-wide MR was used to identify causal relationships between 48 metabolites with ≥3 IVs and 28 complex phenotypes.
source: Univariable metabolome-wide MR (MWMR; Figure 1A) was used to identify causal relationships between 48 metabolites with ≥3 IVs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) and 28 complex phenotypes.
evidence: Description of the metabolite-to-phenotype analysis

claim: The 28 complex phenotypes include a wide range of anthropometric traits, cardiovascular assessments, and blood biomarkers.
source: The latter include a wide range of anthropometric traits, cardiovascular assessments, and blood biomarkers, whose summary statistics originate from the UK Biobank (UKB) (Bycroft et al., 2018;Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: Description of phenotypes analyzed with citation to Bycroft et al., 2018

claim: Summary statistics for the 28 complex phenotypes originate from the UK Biobank (UKB).
source: The latter include a wide range of anthropometric traits, cardiovascular assessments, and blood biomarkers, whose summary statistics originate from the UK Biobank (UKB) (Bycroft et al., 2018;Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: Description of data source with citation to Bycroft et al., 2018

claim: 34 metabolites were associated with at least one phenotype, resulting in 132 unique metabolite-phenotype associations.
source: Overall, 34 metabolites were associated with at least one phenotype (FDR 5% considering all 1344 metabolite-phenotype pairs), resulting in 132 unique metabolite-phenotype associations (Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: Primary finding from the metabolite-to-phenotype analysis

claim: Univariable transcriptome-wide MR was applied to identify associations between expression levels of 10,435 transcripts with ≥3 IVs and the same 28 UKB phenotypes.
source: We applied univariable transcriptome-wide MR (TWMR [Porcu et al., 2019] Figure 1B) to identify associations between expression levels of 10,435 transcripts from the eQTLGen Consortium with ≥3 IVs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) measured in both exposure and outcome datasets and the same 28 UKB phenotypes described in the previous section (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: Description of the transcript-to-phenotype analysis with citation to Porcu et al., 2019

claim: 5140 transcripts associated with at least one phenotype, resulting in 13,141 unique transcript-phenotype associations.
source: In total, 5140 transcripts associated with at least one phenotype (FDR 5% considering all 292,170 gene-phenotype pairs) resulting in 13,141 unique transcript-phenotype associations (Supplementary file 1e).
evidence: Primary finding from the transcript-to-phenotype analysis

claim: The study combined the 133 transcript-metabolite and 132 metabolite-trait associations to pinpoint 216 transcript-metabolite-phenotype causal triplets.
source: We combined the 133 transcript-metabolite (FDR ≤5%) and 132 metabolite-trait (FDR ≤5%) associations to pinpoint 216 transcript-metabolite-phenotype causal triplets (FDR = 1–0.952 = 9.75%) (Supplementary file 1f).
evidence: Description of the mediation analysis approach and its results

claim: Among the 37 triplets for which the transcript and metabolite had previously been linked through automated literature review, none remained after incorporating a third term for the phenotype in the search.
source: Among the 37 triplets for which the transcript and metabolite had previously been linked through automated literature review, none remained after incorporating a third term for the phenotype in the search and manually removing abstracts for which the search terms were used in an erroneous context.
evidence: Result from literature validation analysis

claim: Relaxing the search criteria by omitting the metabolite term, 13/37 (35%) triplets returned at least one match for the gene-trait association.
source: Relaxing the search criteria by omitting the metabolite term, 13/37 (35%) triplets returned at least one match for the gene-trait association.
evidence: Result from literature validation analysis

claim: The TMEM258/FADS1/FADS2 region has >6000 associations reported in the GWAS Catalog as of May 2022.
source: These results align with the known pleiotropy of the region (i.e., >6000 associations reported in the GWAS Catalog as of May 2022).
evidence: External validation from GWAS Catalog database

claim: Involved metabolites are complex lipids synthesized from arachidonic acid.
source: Interestingly, involved metabolites are complex lipids synthesized from arachidonic acid, a product of the rate-limiting enzymes encoded by FADS1 and FADS2 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Based on established biochemical knowledge of lipid metabolism

claim: Arachidonic acid is a product of the rate-limiting enzymes encoded by FADS1 and FADS2.
source: Interestingly, involved metabolites are complex lipids synthesized from arachidonic acid, a product of the rate-limiting enzymes encoded by FADS1 and FADS2 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Based on established biochemical knowledge of fatty acid desaturase function

claim: Polymorphisms affecting the expression of FADS1 and FADS2 were shown to associate with the levels of over 50 complex lipids.
source: Recently, polymorphisms affecting the expression of these genes were shown to associate with the levels of over 50 complex lipids, including the ones identified by our study (Reynolds et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Reynolds et al., 2020

claim: Only 42% (90/216) of the causal triplets showed a significant total transcript-to-phenotype effect estimated by TWMR.
source: Importantly, only 42% (90/216) of the causal triplets showed a significant total transcript-to-phenotype effect (i.e., estimated by TWMR), suggesting that the method lacks power under current settings.
evidence: Quantitative comparison of methods from the study's results

claim: TWMR lacks power under current settings.
source: Importantly, only 42% (90/216) of the causal triplets showed a significant total transcript-to-phenotype effect (i.e., estimated by TWMR), suggesting that the method lacks power under current settings.
evidence: Inference from the observation that 58% of triplets were not detected by TWMR

claim: The gain in power of mediation analysis over TWMR decreases with decreasing mQTL dataset sample sizes.
source: In line with the increased power of mediation analysis with larger mQTL datasets, the gain in power of mediation analysis over TWMR decreases with decreasing mQTL dataset sample sizes (ranging between N = 1000 and N = 4000; Figure 4—figure supplement 2), indicating that our approach is dependent on large sample sizes to reach its full potential.
evidence: Finding from simulation analyses with varying sample sizes

claim: The mediation analysis approach is dependent on large sample sizes to reach its full potential.
source: In line with the increased power of mediation analysis with larger mQTL datasets, the gain in power of mediation analysis over TWMR decreases with decreasing mQTL dataset sample sizes (ranging between N = 1000 and N = 4000; Figure 4—figure supplement 2), indicating that our approach is dependent on large sample sizes to reach its full potential.
evidence: Conclusion from simulation analyses with varying sample sizes

claim: The 126 triplets that were not identified through TWMR represent putative new causal relations.
source: The 126 triplets that were not identified through TWMR due to power issues represent putative new causal relations.
evidence: Inference from the comparison of methods

claim: 48 publications were identified through automated literature review for the association between ANKH and calcium levels.
source: This is well illustrated by a proof-of concept example involving ANKH [MIM: 605145] and calcium levels, for which 48 publications were identified through automated literature review (Supplementary file 1f).
evidence: Result from literature validation analysis

claim: Mutations in ANKH have been associated with several rare mineralization disorders.
source: Mutations in ANKH have been associated with several rare mineralization disorders [MIM: 123000, 118600] (Williams, 2016) due to the gene encoding a transmembrane protein that channels inorganic pyrophosphate to the extracellular matrix, where at low concentrations it inhibits mineralization (Ho et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Williams, 2016 and Ho et al., 2000

claim: ANKH encodes a transmembrane protein that channels inorganic pyrophosphate to the extracellular matrix.
source: Mutations in ANKH have been associated with several rare mineralization disorders [MIM: 123000, 118600] (Williams, 2016) due to the gene encoding a transmembrane protein that channels inorganic pyrophosphate to the extracellular matrix, where at low concentrations it inhibits mineralization (Ho et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ho et al., 2000

claim: Inorganic pyrophosphate at low concentrations inhibits mineralization.
source: Mutations in ANKH have been associated with several rare mineralization disorders [MIM: 123000, 118600] (Williams, 2016) due to the gene encoding a transmembrane protein that channels inorganic pyrophosphate to the extracellular matrix, where at low concentrations it inhibits mineralization (Ho et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ho et al., 2000

claim: A study proposed that ANKH exports ATP to the extracellular space, along with citrate.
source: Recently, a study proposed that ANKH instead exports ATP to the extracellular space (where it is then rapidly converted to inorganic pyrophosphate), along with citrate (Szeri et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Szeri et al., 2020

claim: Citrate has a high binding affinity for calcium.
source: Citrate has a high binding affinity for calcium and influences its bioavailability by complexing calcium-phosphate during extracellular matrix mineralization and releasing calcium during bone resorption (Granchi et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Granchi et al., 2019

claim: Citrate influences calcium bioavailability by complexing calcium-phosphate during extracellular matrix mineralization and releasing calcium during bone resorption.
source: Citrate has a high binding affinity for calcium and influences its bioavailability by complexing calcium-phosphate during extracellular matrix mineralization and releasing calcium during bone resorption (Granchi et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Granchi et al., 2019

claim: The study's data support the role of ANKH in calcium homeostasis through regulation of citrate levels.
source: Together, our data support the role of ANKH in calcium homeostasis through regulation of citrate levels, connecting previously established independent links into a causal triad.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the study's findings and existing literature

claim: Betaine acts as a protective renal osmolyte.
source: This observation is particularly interesting given that betaine acts as a protective renal osmolyte whose plasma and kidney tissue concentration were found to be downregulated in renal ischemia/reperfusion injury (Jouret et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2014) and whose urine levels have been proposed as a biomarker for chronic kidney disease progression (Gil et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jouret et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2014; Gil et al., 2018

claim: Betaine plasma and kidney tissue concentration were found to be downregulated in renal ischemia/reperfusion injury.
source: This observation is particularly interesting given that betaine acts as a protective renal osmolyte whose plasma and kidney tissue concentration were found to be downregulated in renal ischemia/reperfusion injury (Jouret et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2014) and whose urine levels have been proposed as a biomarker for chronic kidney disease progression (Gil et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jouret et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2014

claim: Betaine urine levels have been proposed as a biomarker for chronic kidney disease progression.
source: This observation is particularly interesting given that betaine acts as a protective renal osmolyte whose plasma and kidney tissue concentration were found to be downregulated in renal ischemia/reperfusion injury (Jouret et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2014) and whose urine levels have been proposed as a biomarker for chronic kidney disease progression (Gil et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gil et al., 2018

claim: Renal conditions are commonly monitored through serum creatinine levels.
source: As both renal conditions are commonly monitored through serum creatinine levels, our data support the critical role of osmolyte homeostasis in renal health.
evidence: Based on established clinical practice knowledge

claim: The study's data support the critical role of osmolyte homeostasis in renal health.
source: As both renal conditions are commonly monitored through serum creatinine levels, our data support the critical role of osmolyte homeostasis in renal health.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the study's findings and existing knowledge

claim: While some detected associations were previously reported, a large fraction, especially among the triplets, appears to be novel.
source: Our automated literature review indicates that while some detected associations were previously reported, a large fraction, especially among the triplets, appears to be novel.
evidence: Conclusion from literature validation analysis

claim: The number of previously reported associations is likely underestimated as the automated approach does not account for all synonyms of a given feature.
source: It should be noted that the number of previously reported associations is likely underestimated as our approach does not account for all synonyms of a given feature and requires the terms to appear in the title or abstract of the publication.
evidence: Acknowledgment of methodological limitation

claim: Among the 90 signals that were also identified through TWMR, 93% showed a directionally concordant effect between the transcript-to-phenotype, transcript-to-metabolite, and metabolite-to-phenotype estimates.
source: For instance, among the 90 signals that were also identified through TWMR, 93% showed a directionally concordant effect between the transcript-to-phenotype, transcript-to-metabolite, and metabolite-to-phenotype estimates (i.e., sign of product of the transcript-to-metabolite and metabolite-to-phenotype effects agrees with the sign of the transcript-to-phenotype effect).
evidence: Quantitative validation result from the study's analysis

claim: Dissection of causal effects provides clues as to the molecular mechanism through which involved genes modify complex phenotypes.
source: In these situations, dissection of causal effects provides clues as to the molecular mechanism through which involved genes modify complex phenotypes.
evidence: Conclusion about the utility of the method

claim: While transcript levels of TMEM258/FADS1/FADS2 affected eleven metabolites, three complex lipids were highlighted as strong molecular mediators of the transcript-to-phenotype effects.
source: While transcript levels of these genes affected eleven metabolites, three complex lipids were highlighted as strong molecular mediators of the transcript-to-phenotype effects.
evidence: Specific finding from the study's analysis

claim: A large fraction of detected mediations involves genes encoding metabolic enzymes or transporters/channels.
source: As illustrated through the selected examples, a large fraction of detected mediations involves genes encoding metabolic enzymes or transporters/channels, with an enrichment for 'secondary active transmembrane transporter activity', for example (GO:0015291; FDR=0.021; background: 7884 genes with ≥3 IVs assessed through TWMR; STRING database).
evidence: Finding from enrichment analysis conducted in the study

claim: There is an enrichment for 'secondary active transmembrane transporter activity' (GO:0015291; FDR=0.021) among genes involved in detected mediations.
source: As illustrated through the selected examples, a large fraction of detected mediations involves genes encoding metabolic enzymes or transporters/channels, with an enrichment for 'secondary active transmembrane transporter activity', for example (GO:0015291; FDR=0.021; background: 7884 genes with ≥3 IVs assessed through TWMR; STRING database).
evidence: Statistical result from enrichment analysis using STRING database

claim: The most likely effector genes of mQTLs are enriched for pathway-relevant enzymes and transporters.
source: Matching the finding that the most likely effector genes of mQTLs are enriched for pathway-relevant enzymes and transporters (Smith et al., 2022), these results are not surprising given that the proteins encoded by these genes directly interact with metabolites, making it more likely that the effect of changes in their expression is mediated by metabolites.
evidence: Supported by citation to Smith et al., 2022

claim: Proteins encoded by metabolic enzymes and transporters directly interact with metabolites, making it more likely that the effect of changes in their expression is mediated by metabolites.
source: Matching the finding that the most likely effector genes of mQTLs are enriched for pathway-relevant enzymes and transporters (Smith et al., 2022), these results are not surprising given that the proteins encoded by these genes directly interact with metabolites, making it more likely that the effect of changes in their expression is mediated by metabolites.
evidence: Logical inference based on biochemical knowledge

claim: Interpretation of discovered mediations is limited by the lack of spatial resolution of the mQTL data.
source: While our method is well suited to detect such effects, interpretation of discovered mediations is limited by the lack of spatial resolution of the mQTL data.
evidence: Acknowledgment of methodological limitation

claim: The observation that 77% of the transcript's effect on the phenotype is not mediated by metabolites suggests that either true direct effects are frequent or that other unassessed metabolites or molecular layers play a crucial role in mediation.
source: The observation that 77% of the transcript's effect on the phenotype is not mediated by metabolites suggests that either true direct effects are frequent or that other unassessed metabolites or molecular layers (e.g., proteins, post-translational modifications, etc.) play a crucial role in mediation.
evidence: Interpretation of the study's findings

claim: In the presence of unmeasured mediators or measured mediators without genetic instruments, mediation estimates are lower bounds of the total existing mediation.
source: It is to note that in the presence of unmeasured mediators or measured mediators without genetic instruments, our mediation estimates are lower bounds of the total existing mediation.
evidence: Acknowledgment of methodological limitation based on statistical theory

claim: Unmeasured mediators sharing genetic instruments with the measured ones can modify result interpretation as some of the observed mediators may simply be correlates of the true underlying mediators.
source: In addition, unmeasured mediators sharing genetic instruments with the measured ones can modify result interpretation as some of the observed mediators may simply be correlates of the true underlying mediators.
evidence: Acknowledgment of methodological limitation

claim: Metabolic networks may harbor particularly large number of genetically correlated metabolite species.
source: While this is a limitation of all MR methods, metabolic networks may harbor particularly large number of genetically correlated metabolite species.
evidence: Based on understanding of metabolic network structure

claim: Owing to linkage disequilibrium and regulatory variants affecting multiple genes, transcripts from adjacent genes might appear to be involved in the same signals.
